newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit retreats on selling by U.S. hedge fund.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit retreats on selling by U.S. hedge fund.

text.p: Fresh selling by a U.S. hedge fund with huge long ringgit positions triggered a retreat in the Malaysian unit in the afternoon, dealers said on Friday.
They said the selling started after 0600 GMT and was expected to continue as the hedge fund was rumoured to be in the market to unwind $5-7 billion worth long ringgit positions.
"There is no confirmation about who is behind the selling, but it is a U.S. hedge fund," said a Singapore-based analyst.
He said the hedge fund, which was operating through investment banks in Hong Kong and Singapore, had not yet finished the unwinding.
"It was because of this selling in the last few days that dollar/ringgit could not break below 2.4750," the analyst said.
Dealers said the hedge fund selling reversed the trend in the morning, when buying by some U.S. and Japanese funds against the Singapore dollar helped the ringgit recover.

However, the ringgit retained some of the gains made against the Singapore dollar as funds re-established long ringgit/Sing positions. At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 1.7268/87 a Singapore dollar against 1.7308/27 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
The ringgit was at 2.4840/50 a dollar.
